headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared workspace plus broad plugin/network access; no critical default harm is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can read and ground answers in shared workspace pages, while Semantic Kernel can ingest application context and route outputs through plugins/MCP. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if Notion content is treated as trusted input by the kernel. The pairwise interaction is documented only at the profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes Notion-generated text as instructions without provenance checks
IF a shared workspace page contains attacker-controlled content that Notion summarizes into actionable text
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all Notion-derived text before passing it to Semantic Kernel
Require a human review step before any plugin call triggered by Notion output
Restrict Semantic Kernel plugins to a denylist-free but allowlisted set for 5 minutes of setup
Separate untrusted workspace pages from agent-facing pages
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and Semantic Kernel can read filesystem data, use MCP, and send context to broad model providers. If the pair shares a workspace or application context, sensitive content can flow from Notion into a third-party backend through Semantic Kernel. The profiles do not prove PHI or secrets, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document is available in both the Notion workspace and Semantic Kernel application context
IF Semantic Kernel forwards that content to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or an MCP server
mitigations: Remove sensitive pages from the shared workspace before running the pair
Disable file-reading plugins in Semantic Kernel for the session
Use a local-only model endpoint for the kernel session
Rotate or scope plugin credentials to non-sensitive data
requires-engineering: add data-class filtering before any outbound API call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances, and Semantic Kernel supports multiple instances with shared state via memory stores. Both can write to mutable resources, but the profiles do not show unrestricted write to the same directory or git state. The overlap is real yet not enough for high; uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace or memory store
IF Semantic Kernel plugins write back into pages or databases that Notion AI also edits
mitigations: Assign separate namespaces or folders for each agent
Pause one agent while the other performs writes
Turn off write-capable plugins in Semantic Kernel for the session
Limit Notion AI to read-only tasks during concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI produces grounded workspace text, and Semantic Kernel is a function-calling orchestrator that can act on plugin outputs. If the kernel treats Notion output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions. Because the profiles do not document a verification layer, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Notion output as direct input to a plugin or agent step
IF no verification or citation-checking step is inserted between the agents
mitigations: Require citations on all Notion-derived claims before action
Add a validation prompt before any Semantic Kernel tool call
Route Notion output to a read-only summarizer first
Log and review one sample interaction before enabling automation
requires-engineering: implement structured verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is workspace-bound and vendor-hosted, while Semantic Kernel can send context to broad external providers and MCP servers. That creates a plausible residency or retention mismatch for the same data class, but the profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction or regulated dataset. One-agent citations are sufficient here because the compliance risk is driven by Semantic Kernel's outbound paths.
conditions: IF EU PII or similarly regulated data is processed by Semantic Kernel and sent to a non-approved provider
IF the two agents retain the same data class under different retention policies
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the kernel session
Use only approved providers for the session
Shorten retention settings where configurable
Document the data flow before enabling the pair
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
